overview.headline: How balls fly higher in lunar gravity without drag

keyPoints.point: Students learn that a thrown ball feels no drag on the airless Moon.
keyPoints.quote: so a thrown ball feels no drag at all

keyPoints.point: Students learn that horizontal speed stays constant throughout the flight.
keyPoints.quote: the horizontal speed stays U0 for the whole flight

keyPoints.point: Students learn how vertical speed and height change with time under steady gravity.
keyPoints.quote: The vertical speed is V = V0 - g * t, and the height is y = V0 * t - g * t^2 / 2.

keyPoints.point: Students learn that the highest point follows from the time when vertical velocity reaches zero.
keyPoints.quote: Putting that time into the height equation gives the highest point: ymax = V0^2 / (2 * g).

keyTerms.gloss: Resistance felt by a moving ball that vanishes without air
keyTerms.quote: so a thrown ball feels no drag at all

keyTerms.gloss: Flight with no drag where only weight acts
Downward force that pulls the ball after release
keyTerms.quote: The only force on the ball after it leaves the hand is its weight, which pulls it straight down.

keyTerms.gloss: Steady pull that slows a rising ball
keyTerms.quote: Vertically, gravity slows the ball at a steady rate g.
